statement: For the actual Beatty certificate profile at alpha=log2(3), exact survivor counts through depth 406 and Arb enclosures for 256 atoms give the entire remaining mass in [0.08962961,0.08962962]. The established total-mass identity and positivity imply 0<=F-F_256<=tail; since F_256>=1, the omitted two-thirds moment is at most 2*tail/3. Thus the full integral of F^(2/3) lies in [1.40531077,1.46506386] and the established Minkowski-content formula gives [2.95207917,3.07760004], with decimal endpoints rounded outward. No fitted tail, convergence rate, Hausdorff lower bound or new Lean numerical proof is asserted.

For alpha=log_2 3, the actual normalized certificate counts R_r=r*c_r/binom(m_r-1,r-1) have exactly K=[1,alpha/(alpha-1)] minus the union over j>=1 of (F(delta_j),F(delta_j)+w_j) as their real subsequential limit set. K is nonempty, compact, perfect, Lebesgue-null and has empty interior. Both endpoints of every listed gap are subsequential limits. Every closed interval strictly inside a gap is eventually avoided. Exact phase recurrence is proved; no unproved density or asymptotic input remains. The empirical limiting law is recorded separately. No convergence rate, arbitrary-slope theorem or novelty claim is asserted.

For the full subsequential-limit set K of the actual binomial-normalized certificate counts at alpha=log_2 3, volume(K_epsilon)=2*epsilon+sum_(r>=1) min(w_r,2*epsilon). Positive c,C bound this volume between c*epsilon^(1/3) and C*epsilon^(1/3) for every 0<epsilon<=1/2. The limit of 1-log(volume(K_epsilon))/log(epsilon) as epsilon tends to zero from above is 2/3: Minkowski dimension in the real-line tube convention, with positive finite lower and upper contents. The separate covering-number equivalence is written in the note. No Hausdorff-dimension equality or exact tube leading constant is asserted.

For the actual positive certificate weights at alpha=log_2 3, let N(x)=#{r>=1:w_r>=x}. As x tends to zero from above, x^(2/3)*N(x) tends to A=integral_0^1 (kappa*F(t))^(2/3) dt>0, where kappa=beta*sqrt(beta)/sqrt(2*pi*beta*(1-beta)). The power-transformed sequence (n+1)*w_(n+1)^(2/3) differs from (kappa*F(delta_(n+1)))^(2/3) by a quantity tending to zero. All concrete arithmetic and equidistribution inputs are discharged; no rate is asserted.

For the actual certificate weights at beta=log 2/log 3, r*sqrt(r)*w_r-kappa*F(delta_r) tends to zero, where kappa=beta*sqrt(beta)/sqrt(2*pi*beta*(1-beta)). There exist a,b>0 such that a/(r+1)^(3/2)<=w_(r+1)<=b/(r+1)^(3/2) for every natural r. All counting and asymptotic inputs are discharged; no error rate is asserted.

Any compact real set with an upper metric-tube bound lambda(K_epsilon)<=C*epsilon^(1/3) for 0<epsilon<=1/2 has finite two-thirds Hausdorff measure in the diameter-power convention. In particular the cluster set K of the original binomial-normalized certificate counts at alpha=log_2 3 satisfies H^(2/3)(K)<infinity and dim_H K<=2/3 unconditionally. Maximal separated finite nets give the covering estimate. Positivity of the critical Hausdorff measure and equality of Hausdorff dimension are not asserted without further input.

For m_r=floor(r/beta), the actual certificate weights w_r=M_(m_r+1) beta^r (1-beta)^(m_r-r), r>=1, are positive and sum to 1/terminalRatio. Distinct indices have distinct interior phases and w_1=beta. Their strict cumulative profile is nondecreasing, lies between 1 and 1+1/terminalRatio, has those endpoint traces, and is left-continuous with each right-minus-left jump equal to the corresponding weight.

For the complete cluster set K of the original binomial-normalized integer certificate counts at alpha=log_2 3, epsilon^(-1/3) times Lebesgue measure restricted to its open metric epsilon-neighbourhood converges weakly to dnu(y)=3*2^(1/3)*kappa^(2/3)*y^(2/3) dmu(y). The ordinary uniform tube probabilities converge weakly to y^(2/3) dmu(y)/integral y^(2/3) dmu(y). Every bounded continuous spatial observable has the corresponding normalized moment limit, and every open upper-ray tube volume has its explicit local-content limit. All concrete premises are discharged. No full asymptotic error rate, arbitrary-measurable-set convergence, Hausdorff-dimension equality or extension to arbitrary irrational slopes is asserted.

For the complete subsequential-limit set K of the actual binomial-normalized certificate counts at alpha=log_2 3, the real Lebesgue measure of its open metric epsilon-neighbourhood divided by epsilon^(1/3) tends to the positive finite constant M=3*2^(1/3)*kappa^(2/3)*integral_0^1 F(t)^(2/3) dt. Equivalently M=3*2^(1/3)*kappa^(2/3)*integral y^(2/3) dmu(y) for the proved singular continuous empirical law mu. This is Minkowski measurability in the stated unnormalized real-line tube convention. No self-similarity, bounded-partial-quotient or quantitative equidistribution premise is used. Hausdorff dimension and effective convergence rates are not asserted.

At beta=log 2/log 3, for m_r=floor(r/beta), c_r=minimalCertCount(m_r+1), C_r=binom(m_r-1,r-1), delta_r=r/beta-m_r and F(delta)=1+sum_{delta_j<delta} c_j beta^j (1-beta)^(m_j-j), r*c_r/C_r-F(delta_r) tends to zero as r tends to infinity. No counting, binomial, survivor-phase, first-passage-mass or profile-identification hypothesis remains. The original normalization is checked by an exact binomial identity and a moving quotient estimate. This is qualitative o(1); neither O(r^(-1/2)), arbitrary irrational slopes, numerical tail constants nor integer-trajectory termination is asserted.

Every irrational linear exponential phase has zero limiting Fourier average. For beta=log 2/log 3 this proves that the empirical laws of the exact certificate phases delta_r={r/beta} converge weakly to uniform probability on (0,1]. No equidistribution or Fourier-cancellation premise remains in the concrete theorem.

At the logarithmic slope and every 0<delta<1, including each atom, the full consecutive-survivor transfer (2/a0) s^(-beta delta) [psi(1-beta delta)-(v/2)psi(1-beta delta+beta)] equals the actual cumulative certificate profile 1+sum_{delta_r<delta}w_r. The equality follows by absolutely convergent reindexing and exact total-mass cancellation, so it leaves no undetermined continuous component or additive constant.

For alpha=log_2 3 the empirical probability measures of the actual normalized certificate counts R_r converge weakly to mu=F_*(uniform(0,1]). The same result is proved for averages of every bounded continuous real test function. This probability law is atomless, has a continuous CDF G, gives full mass to the explicit null accumulation set K, and is mutually singular with Lebesgue measure. G(F(t))=t for t in [0,1], and G equals delta_j throughout each closed jump interval [F(delta_j),F(delta_j)+w_j], which has zero mass including its endpoints. Frequencies below every real threshold converge to G, with limit t at F(t). No empirical frequency of exact membership in K, quantitative discrepancy rate or arbitrary-slope certificate theorem is asserted.

Under the explicit uniform phase-hitting premise with constants H>0 and tau>0, the actual certificate cluster set has positive Hausdorff measure at exponent 2/(3*tau), and Hausdorff dimension at least 2/(3*tau). For tau=1, its two-thirds Hausdorff measure is positive and finite and its Hausdorff dimension equals 2/3. These are checked implications: no phase-hitting constant or exponent is supplied for alpha=log_2 3. The consumer audit writes both the original integer count ratios and the fractional phases frac((n+1)/beta) explicitly.

The critical Bernoulli probability of surviving tends to zero and the actual first-descent masses sum to one. Finite last-letter probability and centered-first-moment identities bound surviving endpoint moments by beta. Splitting at a fixed height and using proved normalized survivor decay removes the escape mass. No optional-stopping or first-passage premise is assumed.

For injective phases in (0,1), nonnegative summable weights, 0<q<=1 and q*(1+sum w)=1, let F(t)=1+sum_(phase_i<t) w_i and let g be any bounded continuous real observable. The series of integrals from q^phase_i F(phase_i) to q^phase_i (F(phase_i)+w_i) of g(y)/y has sum (-log(q))*integral_0^1 g(q^t F(t)) dt. Finite cutoff convergence, dominated convergence, summable bounds for primitive increments and exact endpoint cancellation prove the identity. No density of phases or Diophantine condition is required. This formalizes classical occupation calculus for a summable jump profile; it is not an arbitrary-slope theorem for first-passage counts.

A uniform Diophantine lower bound with c>0 and tau>0 for the actual slope 1/beta gives positive Hausdorff measure at exponent 2/(3*tau) and dim_H K>=2/(3*tau) for the original certificate cluster set. A family of such bounds for every tau>1, with constants depending on tau, suffices for dim_H K=2/3. The stronger exponent-one bound gives positive finite two-thirds Hausdorff measure. These are checked conditional implications; neither arithmetic premise is discharged for log_2 3. Dimension equality under the family premise does not assert critical-measure positivity. The consumer expands the original integer counts and every arithmetic quantifier.

For c>0 and tau>0, if c<=q^tau*|q*xi-p| for every positive natural q and integer p, then the positive rotation phases frac((n+1)*xi) satisfy PhaseHittingBound with the same exponent tau and explicit constant H=4^tau/c+1. Dirichlet approximation and the lower bound force a reduced denominator large enough for rational-grid coverage. No such arithmetic constants are supplied for the logarithmic certificate slope.

For sequences of Borel probability measures on metric spaces, weak convergence passes through a measurable map continuous almost everywhere for the limiting measure. Empirical laws are preserved under vanishing real sample errors, and converge on measurable sets with null limiting boundary. These are generic measure-theoretic tools, not a novelty claim.

At beta=log 2/log 3 the strict binomial tail satisfies sqrt(n) T_n/v^n-Phi(n beta)->0 with the exact fractional-part correction. Stirling and a vanishing entropy remainder give the first-term limit; dominated convergence gives the geometric-tail ratio. The actual survivor counts therefore have the explicit convolution phase asymptotic and satisfy the existing MeanderShape predicate unconditionally. The limit is additive o(1), not a quantitative rate.

For the Gamma-normalized law at the logarithmic slope, every chronological tail of the rescaled open jump intervals meets every open neighborhood of every support point. The set S of support-interior values lying in such intervals of arbitrarily large indices is G-delta, has closure equal to the full support interval, has zero Lebesgue measure, and the canonical density is infinite at every point of S. On every open set meeting the support interior, every finite density threshold is exceeded on a positive-Lebesgue-measure subset. Consequently no almost-everywhere equal density version is essentially bounded on such an open set. The proof uses concrete phase recurrence, Baire's theorem, lower semicontinuity and the unit integral, without any additional arithmetic premise. This topology theorem alone gives no L^p classification; the separate concentration and density-integrability rows supply the subcritical range. No literature priority is claimed.

The canonical extended nonnegative occupation density of the concrete Gamma-normalized law is lower semicontinuous. At every positive value contained in rescaled jump intervals of arbitrarily large indices it is infinite, since each contributing interval has the same positive logarithmic kernel there. The full set of infinite-density values has zero Lebesgue measure. This describes the chosen exact density, not continuity or boundedness of a density version.

At beta=log 2/log 3, q=1-beta, m_r=floor(r/beta), c_r=minimalCertCount(m_r+1), delta_r=fract(r/beta) and D_r=Gamma(r/beta)/(r! Gamma(r*q/beta+1)), the original integer counts satisfy c_r/D_r-q^delta_r F(delta_r) -> 0. Equivalently they approach the exactly unit-periodic amplitude B(r/beta), where B(t)=q^fract(t) F(fract(t)). Uniform Gamma interpolation from log-convexity and an exact binomial/Gamma identity discharge the normalization without a phase-convergence or real-variable Stirling premise. D_r is positive for r>0. This is the qualitative concrete specialization of BGL's proposed irrational first-passage amplitude, not a claim of priority, convergence rate or arbitrary-slope formalization.

At beta=log 2/log 3 and q=1-beta, the empirical measures of the actual Gamma-normalized first-passage counts c_r/D_r converge weakly to eta, the image of uniform phase measure under B(t)=q^t F(t). This probability law is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure and mutually singular with the original singular continuous law of F(U). In particular eta(K)=0, its CDF is continuous, and the normalized counts have the prescribed limiting frequency at every real threshold and limiting average for every bounded continuous observable. The proof establishes F'=0 almost everywhere from the null monotone range, then B'=log(q) B nonzero almost everywhere, and proves a null-preimage criterion without global injectivity. No analytic or arithmetic premise remains. The explicit density series is certified by the separate occupation interface; no rate or arbitrary-slope extension is asserted.

At the concrete logarithmic slope, the complete real cluster set of the original Gamma-normalized integer counts equals the support of eta, the closure of the phase-amplitude image and the closure of the union of the rescaled open jump intervals. This is exactly the nondegenerate interval [ell,u], where ell=inf_(r>=1) L_r and u=sup_(r>=1) U_r, with q<=ell<u<=1/q. Every nonempty open interval with endpoints in this support has positive probability, and the CDF is strictly increasing on the support. No numerical endpoint value or finite-index extremum is assumed, and no recurrence or regularity premise remains in the concrete theorem. The consumer expands the original integer counts and both extremal jump formulas.

At the logarithmic slope, write a=-log(q), L_r=q^delta_r F(delta_r) and U_r=q^delta_r (F(delta_r)+w_r). The law eta of q^U F(U) for uniform phase U equals Lebesgue measure with density h(y)=(a*y)^(-1) sum_r 1_(L_r,U_r)(y) for y>0 and zero otherwise. The extended nonnegative density retains overlapping intervals with multiplicity, is finite almost everywhere and integrates to one. The occupation identity holds for every bounded continuous observable, with no analytic or endpoint-mass premise. Its constant-observable specialization proves the convergent series sum_r log(1+w_r/F(delta_r))=-log(q). The consumer also checks convergence of the original Gamma-normalized integer counts to the probability measure defined directly by this density. Exact support and density topology have separate interfaces below; no convergence rate or literature priority is claimed.

The concrete Gamma-normalized limiting law eta is concentrated on the positive compact envelope [q,1/q], and every real power y^p is integrable. For every real p nonzero, the series with terms q^(p*delta_r) ((F(delta_r)+w_r)^p-F(delta_r)^p)/((-log(q))*p) has sum integral y^p d eta, using the actual certificate weights and strict profile values. This includes negative powers without any additional moment hypothesis. The rescaled jump intervals lie in the same envelope. The result is an identity for the limiting law, not an empirical unbounded-observable convergence rate. The exact support interval is identified by the separate support interface.

For a summable nonnegative real sequence w, N(x)=#{n:w_n>=x} is finite for x>0 and sum_n min(w_n,t)=integral_0^t N(x) dx for every t>0. If x^(2/3)*N(x)->A as x decreases to zero, then t^(-1/3)*sum_n min(w_n,t)->3*A, including the identically zero sequence. The original interface with the additional w_0>0 premise remains available. This generic classical layer-cake implication requires no monotonicity of w and no error rate.

If K is a closed interval [a,b] minus pairwise disjoint open gaps of summable nonnegative lengths w_n, all gap and envelope endpoints belong to K, and sum w_n=b-a, then the real Lebesgue volume of its open metric epsilon-neighbourhood is 2*epsilon+sum_n min(w_n,2*epsilon) for every epsilon>0. This is a generic classical gap formula, not a novelty claim.

The finite measure dnu(y)=3*2^(1/3)*kappa^(2/3)*y^(2/3) dmu(y), where mu is the actual singular certificate law, has total mass equal to the previously proved positive Minkowski content. Its probability normalization has exact measurable-set and integral formulas dnu_hat(y)=y^(2/3) dmu(y)/integral y^(2/3) dmu(y). All scale constants cancel in this normalization; its connection to actual metric tubes is proved in J-beatty-certificate-local-content.

For distinct atoms in (0,1) with summable nonnegative weights, the closure of the cumulative jump profile range is its envelope minus the pairwise disjoint open jump intervals, and this complement has zero Lebesgue measure. Dense strictly positive atoms make the profile strictly increasing and the range closure perfect. Recurrent phase sampling has exactly that range closure as its real subsequential limit set; an additive error tending to zero preserves all such limits. These are generic pure-jump consequences, not a novelty claim.

The moving-cutoff asymptotic is stable under vanishing perturbations for nonnegative sequences and nonnegative monotone ceilings, including ceilings that vanish. For each real spatial threshold y, retain the actual certificate weight w_r exactly when y<F(delta_r). Then x^(2/3) times the number of retained weights at least x tends, as x decreases to zero, to integral_0^1 1_{y<F(t)}*(kappa*F(t))^(2/3) dt. Empty retained families are allowed. No new arithmetic or equidistribution premise is imposed on the concrete certificate sequence.

For a null subset K of [a,b] given by removing pairwise disjoint open gaps with summable nonnegative lengths w_n and left endpoints l_n, with every gap and envelope endpoint retained in K, define S_epsilon(y)=sum_{y<l_n} min(w_n,2*epsilon). For every epsilon>0 and real y, S_epsilon(y)<=lambda(K_epsilon intersect (y,infinity))<=S_epsilon(y)+4*epsilon. The bound accounts for at most one crossing gap and the two exterior collars. It is a geometric comparison error, not an effective rate for the limiting measure.

For an equidistributed sequence theta_n in [0,1) and a monotone real g with g(0)>=0, T^(-1) times the number of indices n>=0 satisfying n+1<=T*g(theta_n) tends to integral_0^1 g. If g(0)>0 the same limit holds for any bounded-above sequence u_n with u_n-g(theta_n)->0. The proof uses finite phase partitions, dilated prefix frequencies and Darboux sums; dense jumps are permitted. Positive certificate phases satisfy the required interval frequencies without an added equidistribution premise.

For H>0 and tau>0, assume every 0<=a<b<=1 contains an actual certificate phase delta_(n+1) with (n+1)*(b-a)^tau<=H. Then the actual certificate CDF is globally Holder with exponent 2/(3*tau) and a finite constant. Its image of the certificate cluster set is exactly [0,1]. The proof combines the positive three-halves weight lower bound with the exact CDF plateau at both endpoints of every gap. The quantitative phase-hitting premise is explicit and is not proved for the logarithmic slope; qualitative equidistribution does not discharge it.

For fixed irrational 1<alpha<2, beta=1/alpha, q=1-beta, B=alpha^alpha/(alpha-1)^(alpha-1), m_r=floor(alpha*r), delta_r={alpha*r}, and the binary first-descent counts c_r=M_(m_r+1), the written proof gives R+_r=F(delta_r)+O(r^(-1/2)) with F(delta)=1+sum_{delta_j<delta} w_j and w_j=c_j/(B^j*q^delta_j)=c_j*beta^j*q^(m_j-j). The total weight is 1/(alpha-1), and the first jump is beta. The argument imports the classical positive-partial-sum generating identity, proves a non-circular n^(-3/2) coefficient bound, constructs the survivor profile by an absolutely convergent moving-phase convolution, and controls its remainder. The centered Bernoulli walk fixes the total mass. This is a new written proof for independent review, not an end-to-end Lean theorem; the published paper and older conjecture labels are not retagged. No priority or termination claim.

Exact survivor counts through depth 8000 give 5047 crossing orders. The independent binomial-tail identity n*N_n=sum_{k=1}^n T_k*N_(n-k) holds through depth 256. Numerical atom weights agree in entropy and centered-Bernoulli coordinates; the first eight are approximately 0.630929754, 0.146916662, 0.185388186, 0.064753517, 0.095328147, 0.038053482, 0.022152587, 0.039600725. Head comparisons and an actual-run provenance manifest are recorded. Floating-point phases, weights and residuals are diagnostics, not certified enclosures or a proof of convergence.

The Beatty crossing hypotheses alpha>1, delta=alpha*r-m in (0,1) give the two exact fractional-part coordinates. For the existing survivor and minimal-certificate counts, consecutive scaled survivor jumps cancel to the certificate count; finite-depth normalization and additive error control are exact. For any nonnegative summable weights on distinct real phases, the strict cumulative series is monotone, has the stated one-sided traces and jumps exactly equal to the weights; its endpoint traces follow when all phases lie in (0,1). A moving-kernel limit follows under explicit summability, uniform domination, fixed-index approximation and vanishing-remainder hypotheses. These analytic hypotheses are not discharged for the concrete count sequence in Lean. The module compiles; an executed audit of eleven principal declarations uses only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

For any real xi and reduced rational r with |xi-r|<=1/r.den^2, every phase interval 0<=a<b<=1 with r.den*(b-a)>4 contains frac(n*xi) at an index 0<n<r.den. The proof uses coprimality to enumerate the rational grid and explicitly keeps the perturbed point away from both endpoints. This is a classical rational-grid argument, formalized as the input to quantitative certificate phase hitting.

For nonnegative terminal A and u the coefficients of exp(sum_{n>=1} A_n X^n/n), Lean proves A_n/n<=u_n without a summability premise. A terminal bound A_n<=K/sqrt(n) for n>0 gives u_n<=U/(n sqrt(n)) for some finite U>=0. If also a/sqrt(n)<=A_n, the matching bound a/(n sqrt(n))<=u_n follows, so positive a gives sharp three-halves order without any phase-limit assumption. The recurrence with u_0=1 uniquely characterizes the formal exponential coefficients even without positivity. These are theorems about formal coefficients; the actual survivor-count identity and coarse terminal estimates are not proved here.

For a nonnegative summable real sequence u satisfying n*u_n=sum_{j<n} A_(n-j)*u_j, a square-root bound on A implies a three-halves bound on u by strong induction; coefficient decay is not an input. If sqrt(n)*A_n-Phi(n*beta) tends to zero for bounded Phi, then n*sqrt(n)*u_n-sum_j u_j*Phi((n-j)*beta) tends to zero. Lean proves fixed-lag passage, uniform near-half domination and a concrete far-half Cesaro bound. No continuity of Phi or quantitative error rate is asserted; the concrete counting recurrence is not established by this module.

For nonnegative A, let u be the coefficients of the formal exponential exp(sum_{n>=1} (A_n/n) X^n). If Phi is bounded and sqrt(n)*A_n-Phi(n*beta) tends to zero, then n*sqrt(n)*u_n-sum_j u_j*Phi((n-j)*beta) tends to zero. The formal chain rule proves the recurrence, factorial-weighted convolution powers prove summability, and the renewal theorem supplies coefficient decay and the moving limit. Neither summability nor a vanishing remainder is assumed in the final theorem. This is an analytic theorem about formal exponential coefficients, not an identification of those coefficients with survivor counts or a quantitative error estimate.

For the existing natural-number survivor counts N_n=neverNegCount n and strict positive-endpoint binomial counts T_n=endpointCount n, n*N_n=sum_{j<n} T_(n-j)*N_j for every n>=0, with no counting or asymptotic premise. Consequently SurvivorExponentialIdentity holds for the actual normalized counts. The proof retains the odd-letter polynomial variable, uses the exact last-letter survivor/first-descent partition, preserves endpoint support under formal inversion and Euler differentiation, and separates the logarithmic derivatives. The strict threshold is checked using the inequality between positive powers of two and powers of three. This is a formalization of the classical counting identity, with no priority or trajectory-termination claim.

For the existing survivor counts and strict terminal binomial counts, SurvivorExponentialIdentity is equivalent to the natural-number recurrence n*N_n=sum_{j<n} T_(n-j)*N_j at every degree. This proves an equivalence, not the recurrence. Assuming that identity and coarse two-sided square-root bounds on normalized T_n yields two-sided three-halves bounds on normalized N_n, without the terminal phase-asymptotic hypothesis. Separately, assuming summability of normalized N_n, the explicit survivor profile differs from its first N summands by at most a0/(1-s) times the remaining normalized coefficient mass, uniformly over every real phase including jumps. Finite truncations therefore converge uniformly; no explicit numerical cutoff or tail constant is supplied.

At the existing logarithmic slope beta, define the strict terminal binomial count, normalize it and the actual neverNegCount by v=2*rateBase, and define survivorPhase(x)=sum_j (N_j/v^j)*terminalPhase(x-j*beta), with terminalPhase(x)=a0*s^(1-fract(x))/(1-s). Under the two named hypotheses SurvivorExponentialIdentity and EndpointPhaseAsymptotic, Lean proves summability, the additive survivor phase limit, profile periodicity and positive lower and finite upper bounds, and the existing PaperBSurvivorAsymptotic.MeanderShape predicate for this explicit profile. The two hypotheses are propositions passed as arguments, not axioms or proved inputs. The actual counting identity, terminal asymptotic, full certificate jump-series identification, total mass and quantitative O(r^(-1/2)) estimate are not discharged by this conditional theorem; existing unconditional paper claims are unchanged.

At beta=log 2/log 3 and v=2*rateBase, the actual strict endpoint count T_n lies between binom(n,floor(n*beta)+1) and 5/2 times that first term for every n>0. Global Stirling bounds, a bounded entropy correction and the finite initial segment prove positive two-sided square-root bounds on T_n/v^n. Together with the proved actual counting identity, there exist a,U>0 such that a/(n*sqrt(n))<=N_n/v^n<=U/(n*sqrt(n)) for every n>0. Equivalently the existing survivorDensity is Theta[atTop] of the existing model rateBase^n*n^(-3/2), unconditionally. The normalized survivor sequence is also summable, discharging the premises of the existing profile-bound and uniform-truncation theorems. No phase-limit, counting or terminal-bound hypothesis remains in the sharp-order theorem. The constants are existential. The finer phase and certificate identification are proved in subsequent ledger entries; the quantitative rate remains separate. This counts parity words, not integer trajectories.

For real probability measures indexed by a countably generated filter, convergence of the mass of every open upper ray to that of a fixed probability measure implies weak convergence. For finite measures, convergence of every open upper-ray mass together with convergence of total mass to a nonzero finite limiting measure implies weak convergence. The proof uses differences of tails on half-open intervals and the Portmanteau theorem. These are general classical measure-theoretic implications.

The model tail sum_(n>N) n^(-3/2) is at most 2*N^(-1/2) for positive N. If a summable sequence w has positive two-sided bounds a*(n+1)^(-3/2)<=w_n<=b*(n+1)^(-3/2), then (min(a,1)/2)*t^(1/3)<=sum_n min(w_n,t)<=(2+2*b)*t^(1/3) for every 0<t<=1. These generic estimates use an integral test and finite blocks, with no monotonicity assumption on w itself.

At the logarithmic slope, the actual Gamma limiting law eta satisfies eta(A)<=C lambda(A)^(1/3) for every measurable set of finite Lebesgue measure, with one positive constant C. Its CDF is globally one-third Holder. The canonical extended density satisfies lambda{h>T}<=D T^(-3/2) for every positive threshold with one positive constant D, hence belongs to weak L^(3/2). These bounds use the explicit occupation formula, positive envelope and chronological three-halves jump-length bound, with no additional spacing hypothesis. No optimal exponent or convergence rate is claimed.

For every real exponent 1<=p<3/2, the canonical Gamma-law density has finite integral of h^p against Lebesgue measure, retaining its exceptional infinite values. Its real representative h.toReal belongs to MemLp at exponent ofReal(p); assigning zero at infinite values changes only a null set. These are powers of the density, not moments of the random variable. The explicit density series and all exponent quantifiers are expanded in the consumer audit. Membership at p=3/2 or above is not established by this Lean statement; a separate written arithmetic argument extends the range to p<62/41.

The actual Gamma-law CDF fails every finite Lipschitz bound on every open set meeting the interior of its exact support interval. This is compatible with the global one-third Holder estimate. The proof uses positive density superlevels and lower semicontinuity to force an interval with probability mass exceeding a proposed Lipschitz increment bound. No differentiability premise is assumed and optimality of the Holder exponent is not asserted.

The dense null G-delta constructed from chronological jump tails is the entire infinite-value set of the canonical Gamma-law density. It has zero s-dimensional Hausdorff measure for every real s>2/3 and Hausdorff dimension at most 2/3, without an arithmetic assumption. Tail covers and summable s-powers of the rescaled jump lengths prove the bound. Its closure is the full support interval. No matching lower dimension bound is claimed; this exceptional set is distinct from the original binomial-normalized cluster set K.

For the actual Gamma-law jump intervals I_r=(L_r,U_r), the extended integral of (sum_r 1_(I_r))^2 equals the ordered sum of all pair-intersection lengths, including infinite values. Since the density is this multiplicity times 1/(a*y) on a positive compact envelope, its extended square integral is finite if and only if the overlap energy is finite; equivalently its almost-everywhere real representative belongs to L2. The full min/max endpoint sum is expanded in a seven-record consumer audit allowing only standard Lean axioms. This is an exact criterion, not an assertion that either finiteness condition holds; the arithmetic strengthening is recorded separately as a written proof.
